units.normalized_text: Team, we need a direction on the AI assistant for support tickets. Build in-house or buy? I'd like a recommendation ready for the Nov 12 steering meeting.
I've looked at two vendors, Relay and Hollis. Relay is my pick. It plugs into our ticketing tool out of the box.
Third option is to build it ourselves on the LLM API we already pay for. I could prototype quickly.
Honestly I'd lean to build. We'd own the roadmap.
Before we go further, what's the budget? I need year one numbers.
Finance gave us a cap of $200k for year one, all in.
Confirming: $200k cap, all in, including implementation.
Pricing as I have it: Relay $180k a year, Hollis $240k a year.
Then Hollis is over the cap before any implementation fee. I can't support Hollis.
OK, that takes Hollis off the table unless the price changes.
On build: I'd need two engineers for two quarters, and I don't have two free until Q3.
That's a problem. We want this live before the January peak, ideally by Jan 15.
Fine, I'm dropping build. It can't make Jan 15.
So it's Relay, assuming it checks out. Jonas, what do we know about their security?
They have SOC 2 Type II. It's on their website.
I looked at their trust page this morning. It says Type I, with Type II in progress. Those are not the same thing.
Hm, maybe I misread it. I'll ask their rep.
Bigger issue: our EU customer contracts require ticket data to stay in the EU. Does Relay have an EU region?
I think so but I'm not sure. I'll ask.
On the EU point, yes, it's in the enterprise agreements, clause 9. I can confirm that.
So the conditions are SOC 2 Type II evidence and an EU data region. Anything else?
From legal, we need a signed DPA before any ticket data goes to them.
Noted.
Quick check on Relay's number. Does the $180k include implementation?
Don't know. Their quote says "platform license". I'll ask.
Update from Relay's rep: the SOC 2 Type II audit report will be available Dec 1. Type I is done.
Then I can't approve data going to Relay before Dec 1. I could support picking Relay on Nov 12 if go-live is gated on that report.
Does that still work for Jan 15?
Yes, if the report lands Dec 1 with no major findings.
Pricing update: implementation is a separate one-time $35k. So $215k in year one.
That's over the cap, $215k against $200k, unless we negotiate.
Can we get the implementation fee down?
I'll push procurement to waive or split the $35k. I can support Relay if we land at or under $200k. Otherwise it needs an exception.
Keiko, what would Hollis cost with implementation? Just for comparison.
$240k plus $50k implementation, so $290k. Way out.
Unrelated, who's presenting at the Nov all-hands? Nothing on the schedule yet.
No idea, not me.
Don't look at me.
Let's take that offline. Back to Relay.
My view: Relay. I support it. Keiko?
Yes, Relay. I support it.
I'm fine with Relay as long as the SOC 2 Type II report lands. That's my condition too.
Same as I said. Conditional on the report and the EU region.
Yes to Relay at or under $200k.
Ben?
Legal is OK with Relay as long as the DPA is signed before go-live. I'll send redlines to their counsel by Nov 6.
Thanks. Where we are: the preference is Relay. Open items are the Type II report on Dec 1, EU region confirmation, the implementation fee, and the DPA. Right?
Right.
Yes. I'll confirm the EU region with their rep by Friday.
And I'll chase the audit report and ask for a draft earlier.
I'll talk to procurement about the fee by Nov 5.
OK. I'll take this to Nov 12 as a conditional recommendation. Thanks all.
ok
